pose-vs-remplissage.answerHeading: Nail extensions vs fill in Sainte-Foy: which service is right for you?
pose-vs-remplissage.answerBlock: Choose a full set when your natural nails are bare — either because you have never had extensions before or because your previous set was removed. Choose a fill when your existing extensions are still in good shape and three to four weeks have passed since your last appointment.
pose-vs-remplissage.body: At Ongles et Spa Québec, located at Place de la Cité on boulevard Laurier, our technicians welcome clients from across the west end of Québec City: residents of Sainte-Foy, Sillery, Cap-Rouge, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, and surrounding communities. Knowing the difference between a full set and a fill helps you plan your visits and budget your nail care with confidence. A full set is your starting appointment. Your technician prepares the natural nail surface, applies a tip extension if you want added length, and covers everything with gel or acrylic depending on your preference. She then shapes, smooths, and finishes with your chosen colour or nail art design. A full set typically takes between 90 and 120 minutes. A full set is also the right choice when your current set is more than five weeks old or too worn to be repaired — starting fresh gives your natural nails a chance to breathe and ensures the cleanest result. A fill is your regular maintenance visit, scheduled every three to four weeks. As your natural nail grows, a gap appears at the base of each extension. Your technician fills that gap with fresh product, re-shapes the curve of each nail, and updates the colour. A fill takes approximately 60 to 90 minutes. Waiting more than five weeks between fills increases the risk of lifting, which can trap moisture and eventually weaken the natural nail beneath. Our technicians at Place de la Cité assess your nails on arrival and recommend the most appropriate service. Walk-ins are welcome every day at our Sainte-Foy location.

manucure-vs-pedicure.answerHeading: Manicure vs pedicure in Sainte-Foy: what is the difference?
manucure-vs-pedicure.answerBlock: A manicure is devoted to your hands, cuticles, and fingernails, finishing with a massage and your choice of polish. A pedicure provides the same focused care for your feet and toenails, with the added benefit of a relaxing foot soak and a heel scrub. Both services are performed daily at Place de la Cité and are easy to combine in one visit.
manucure-vs-pedicure.body: At Ongles et Spa Québec in the heart of Place de la Cité, our technicians take equal pride in hand and foot care. Whether you come in for a quick hand refresh or a deeply relaxing pedicure, you leave with results that look great and feel wonderful. Here is a complete breakdown of each service to help you choose. A manicure begins with a warm hand soak that softens the skin around your nails. Your technician carefully removes or pushes back cuticles, then files and shapes your nails to the style you prefer — square, round, oval, almond, or coffin. A moisturizing hand lotion is massaged in before your chosen polish is applied. A manicure takes about 45 minutes and is an excellent routine for anyone who wants their hands to look polished at work, at social events, or simply every day. A pedicure starts with a warm, relaxing foot soak that relieves tired feet after a long day on your feet. Your technician then exfoliates the heels and removes calluses, shapes and buffs the toenails, and performs a foot and lower-leg massage with a rich moisturizing balm. The appointment closes with your choice of nail polish. A pedicure takes about 60 minutes and is especially popular during summer months when open-toe shoes are part of the daily wardrobe. If you are undecided between the two, think about what your next week looks like. An important presentation or meeting? Prioritize a manicure. A weekend by the river or at the beach? Book a pedicure for beautifully groomed toenails. Many clients from Sainte-Foy, Sillery, and Cap-Rouge book both services in a single visit. Ask us about our combined appointment options.

gel-vs-acrylique.answerHeading: Gel vs acrylic nails in Sainte-Foy: which system suits you best?
gel-vs-acrylique.answerBlock: At Ongles et Spa Québec, we offer both gel and acrylic — two professional nail systems, each with distinct strengths. Gel is admired for its natural, glossy finish and flexible feel. Acrylic is prized for its exceptional firmness and resistance to everyday wear. Our technicians at Place de la Cité are trained in both and will guide you to the right choice.
gel-vs-acrylique.body: The gel versus acrylic question comes up often at our Sainte-Foy salon, and it is one we enjoy answering because both systems produce beautiful, long-lasting results. The right choice depends on your nails, your habits, and your aesthetic preferences. Gel is a liquid or semi-solid product that hardens under UV or LED light. After curing, it has a smooth, slightly flexible feel that many clients find very comfortable. The finish is glossy and natural-looking, and the colour stays vibrant and chip-resistant for weeks. Gel is odourless during application and is a popular choice for first-time clients and those who prefer a subtler, everyday look. Gel requires a fill about every three weeks to maintain a clean appearance at the base. Acrylic is made by combining a powder and a liquid monomer that harden together when exposed to air. Once set, acrylic is firm and very resilient — it handles physical impacts from daily tasks better than gel in most situations. This makes it an excellent choice for active clients, those with naturally brittle nails, and anyone who wants longer extensions. Acrylic is also easier to sculpt into dramatic or elongated shapes. It soaks off cleanly and needs a fill every three to four weeks. At our Sainte-Foy salon, our technicians use sterilized or single-use tools for every client, maintaining the highest hygiene standards in the region. Visit us at Place de la Cité on boulevard Laurier for a personal consultation. Our team will examine your natural nails and recommend the system that will work best for your lifestyle.

meilleur-pour.answerHeading: Which nail service is best suited to your lifestyle in Sainte-Foy?
meilleur-pour.answerBlock: For lasting results that hold up through daily activities, gel or acrylic extensions lasting three to four weeks are the clear winner. For consistent natural nail upkeep, a manicure every two weeks is the ideal routine. For a wedding, gala, or any special occasion where your nails will be noticed, a full set with custom nail art is our top recommendation.
meilleur-pour.body: At Ongles et Spa Québec, we believe that the best nail service is the one that fits your real life — your schedule, your occasion, and your hands. Whether you are discovering nail care for the first time or looking for the most durable option for an active lifestyle, this guide will help you choose with confidence. For durability across a busy daily routine, gel or acrylic extensions are unbeatable. Both systems remain chip-free for three to four weeks even through demanding schedules. Acrylic is especially resilient for clients who work with their hands, enjoy sports, or simply need nails that can keep up. Gel offers a subtler, more natural-looking finish that blends beautifully into professional and social settings alike. For special occasions — weddings, engagement parties, holiday galas, graduation ceremonies, or family photo shoots — a full set with custom nail art elevates any look. Our technicians at Ongles et Spa Québec design bespoke nail art including floral details, colour gradients, crystal accents, and intricate freehand patterns. Allow 90 minutes to two hours for a full nail art appointment, and consider booking a few days before your event. For regular maintenance of natural, unextended nails, a manicure every two weeks keeps your hands looking polished and your cuticles healthy. A pedicure every three to four weeks, especially during warm-weather months, keeps your feet soft and your toenails neatly groomed. Clients from across the west end of Québec City — Sainte-Foy, Sillery, Cap-Rouge — come to Place de la Cité regularly for our combination of quality, hygiene, and flexibility. Walk-ins are welcome every day. Book online or simply come in.
